articles.title: New Trailer for OWN Documentary on All-Black Women's Volleyball Team Drops Ahead of Premiere Date
articles.summary: "We Belong Here: The Story of Team Dream," a documentary chronicling the first-ever all-Black women's professional volleyball team, will debut on the Oprah Winfrey Network on Saturday, September 26 at 9 p.m. ET.
articles.body:
"We Belong Here: The Story of Team Dream," a documentary chronicling the first-ever all-Black women's professional volleyball team, will debut on the Oprah Winfrey Network on Saturday, September 26 at 9 p.m. ET.

"Told entirely through the voices of the women themselves, with no external narrator, 'We Belong Here: The Story of Team Dream,' is a story of triumph. The film honors the athletes' resilience, joy, humor, friendship, and pride, while acknowledging the systemic barriers they faced. At its heart, it is a story about determination, community, and the power of belonging."

As noted in the release, the team was led by former Texas volleyball superstar, two-time AVCA First Team All American and NCAA national champion Haley Eckerman.

The team had "limited practice," per the release. However, that didn't stop Team Dream from a dominant performance. Team Dream went 7-0 overall, winning gold in the five-team tournament .

It wasn't easy all along the way. Team Dream had a pair of tough five-set matches in the playoff bracket, especially in the semifinals, when the squad was down two sets to zero against Team Freedom. However, Team Dream rallied for the 3-2 win before doing the same against Hoosier Exterminators for the triumphant victory.

The documentary, which was produced by Bunim/Murray Productions (a Banijay Americas company), has already premiered at the Martha's Vineyard African American Film Festival.

articles.title: Barry Melrose, hockey player and coach-turned-broadcaster, dies at 70
articles.summary: Melrose stepped away from his analyst role in 2023 after he was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.
articles.body: Barry Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died. He was 70. ESPN announced Melrose’s death Wednesday after his wife informed the network. “From the flowing locks of his distinctive mullet to the flared lapels of his trademark long suit coats, Barry Melrose cut an unmistakable figure whenever you were fortunate enough to run into him at a rink or catch him on your television screen,” NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman said. “You were even more fortunate if you engaged him in conversation or listened to his analysis because he never failed to boost your love of the game of hockey.” Melrose stepped away from his analyst role in 2023 after being diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. Wayne Gretzky at the time said Melrose was “bigger than any team.” Melrose had a relatable everyman’s broadcasting style, bringing a sense of humor to his insights, and was easily recognized by his goatee and slicked-back hair. “For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey,” ESPN said in a statement. “His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing and his passion was unmistakable.” From rural Kelvington, Saskatchewan, Melrose broke into pro hockey with the Cincinnati Stingers of the now-defunct World Hockey Association in 1976. He played three seasons in Cincinnati — the last teaming with a young Mark Messier — and, following the WHA’s demise, made the transition to the NHL with Winnipeg in 1979. Melrose went on to play for Toronto and Detroit, where he closed his career following the 1985-86 season. He finished with 10 goals and 33 points and 728 penalty minutes in 300 career NHL regular-season games, and he skated in seven more in the playoffs. His WHA totals were five goals and 32 points and 343 penalty minutes in 178 games with Cincinnati. Melrose turned to coaching and led the Adirondack Red Wings to win the American Hockey League Calder Cup championship in 1992. The following year, Melrose was hired by the Kings, where he brought a sense of colorful flair and instant success to Los Angeles. In his rookie season, he coached a Kings team that featured Gretzky to make a memorable playoff run. They reached the final before losing to Montreal in five games. Melrose finished with a record of 79-101 and 29 ties over two-plus seasons in L.A. before being fired midway through the 1994-95 season. He was hired by ESPN in 1996 and left broadcasting for what became a brief stint coaching the Tampa Bay Lightning in Steven Stamkos’ rookie season in 2008-09. Melrose was fired 16 games into the season following a 5-7-4 start and returned to broadcasting. Melrose also was known for his long-ball hitting prowess in fast-pitch softball, joining fellow Kelvington-area NHL players Wendel Clark, Joey Kocur, Kelly Chase and Kevin Kaminski and others in the offseason in Saskatchewan to form what some call “the toughest team there ever was.”

articles.title: Avinash Sable eyes Asian Games double, 5,000m qualification in Indian Athletics Series final
articles.summary: More sports News: New Delhi: With an Asian Games double in his sights, Avinash Sable will put his steeplechase skills to the test at the Indian Athletics Series final h.
articles.body: New Delhi: With an Asian Games double in his sights, Avinash Sable will put his steeplechase skills to the test at the Indian Athletics Series final here on Thursday while also chasing the 5,000m qualification mark of 13:39.18 seconds.The Athletics Federation of India (AFI) is seeking approval from the Aichi-Nagoya Games organisers for Sable to contest the 5,000m alongside his confirmed 3,000m steeplechase event. But the Hangzhou Asian Games gold medallist must first breach the AFI qualification mark at the JLN stadium.“I am looking forward to evaluating my skills in Thursday’s race before the Japan Asian Games,” Sable said on Wednesday. “Negotiating water jumps in the steeplechase race is an important part of the strategy,” he added.It has been nearly 14 months since the national record holder last competed in the gruelling event featuring seven water barriers and 28 fixed hurdles. Sable suffered an injury at the 2025 Monaco Diamond League and has since undergone rehabilitation.“I’m mentally and physically strong enough to face any challenge during the Games,” he said. Sable won steeplechase gold and 5,000m silver at the Hangzhou Games in 2023 and hopes to win two medals in Japan. His national record is 8:09.91, set at the 2024 Paris Diamond League.Attention will also be on the quartermilers and the women’s 4x400m team.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IOA forms committee to probe Asunta Lakra’s harassment charge
articles.summary: Hockey News: Kolkata: Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha’s decision to constitute an independent inquiry committee to examine former India women’s .
articles.body: Kolkata: Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha’s decision to constitute an independent inquiry committee to examine former India women’s hockey captain Asunta Lakra’s complaint has been welcomed by Hockey India (HI) executive board member and vice-president Asima Ali, who called for “strict and immediate action” against those found responsible.Lakra had alleged in her email to Union sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and TOPS officials in July that, after informing the Jharkhand govt about allegations of sexual harassment against former Eklavya Hockey Centre coach Sudhir Golla, she was threatened by HI secretary general and Hockey Jharkhand president Bhola Nath Singh for speaking up.“It’s a great step. I’m very happy with what Ma’am PT Usha has done. It should have been done earlier, but at least they have done it now. Strict and immediate action should be taken against the culprits,” Ali said.In a letter dated Sept 7, IOA informed HI that it had constituted the committee following the federation’s request to the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports on July 15 and the ministry’s subsequent request to IOA on July 16.The committee will be chaired by retired Justice Deepa Sharma, with Vandana Rao, Mamta Kharb and Sitwat Nabi as members. IOA said the committee would function independently and impartially. HI has been asked to bear the committee’s honorarium and expenses, including travel, accommodation and incidental expenses.IOA president Usha’s letter to HI also stated, “Hockey India is also requested to extend its full cooperation to the Committee and to ensure that all relevant records, documents, information and such other assistance as may be required are made available to the Committee in a timely manner, so as to enable it to discharge its mandate effectively and expeditiously.”Ali said she would extend her full support to the committee and cooperate with its proceedings. “The committee has my complete support. Asunta is also there. I don’t know about the rest,” she said.The HI vice-president also criticised attempts to silence people within the sport before adding, “Bhola Nath should be investigated for allegedly using Hockey India funds for the case that I have filed against him in the Delhi High Court, and the amount should be recovered immediately by Hockey India.”Singh has already denied the allegations made by Lakra, calling them baseless. Golla has also rejected the allegations and demanded a fair inquiry.The dispute between HI and Lakra took a further turn when HI’s Ethics Committee, headed by retired Justice Raghvendra Kumar, initiated a fact-finding inquiry into complaints filed against Lakra by Jharkhand player Albela Rani Toppo. Lakra termed the move “intimidation” and urged the sports minister to intervene and stop the Ethics Committee inquiry against her.With IOA now setting up an independent committee to examine Lakra’s allegations, the focus will be on whether the inquiry brings clarity to the competing complaints and establishes accountability.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Noah Lyles eyes 2028 Olympic title defence after injury ends season
articles.summary: More sports News: Noah Lyles wasn’t planning on playing ‘commentator’ ahead of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship.The reigning men’s Olympic 100m champ.
articles.body: Noah Lyles wasn’t planning on playing ‘commentator’ ahead of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship.The reigning men’s Olympic 100m champion had been looking forward to joining the sport’s biggest stars at World Athletics’ new season-ending showpiece in Budapest, until injury forced him to end his season early.In a video call with reporters on Tuesday, Lyles grinned when he was asked a couple of times for his views on some of his rivals who will be in action this weekend. “Shoot, I usually focus more on myself than other people,” Lyles said in response to a question about his American compatriot Kenny Bednarek attempting the sprint double in Budapest. When the very next question was about what impression he had of some of the South African sprinters, the 29-year-old smiled again while going on to say, “I’m not here to be a commentator of sorts today. That’s not really my goal.”And then came a question about 2027. The conversation was about Noah Lyles once again. And the four-time 200m world champion was only too happy to look ahead to what he considers the ‘building blocks’ in his quest to defend his Olympic 100m crown on home soil in Los Angeles.“I am very excited for 2027. It’s going to be a lot of fun,” Lyles said. “2027 is the building block for 2028. And let’s get that plan smooth and polished so that when we go into 2028, we’re just following the blueprint because we know it’s going to work.”Though he sustained his season-ending injury at the US nationals in July, Lyles managed to run two 9.7-second races at the event before the setback, leaving even himself a little ‘shocked’.“I don’t like to put limits on myself,” Lyles said. “In my head, American records definitely come in touching the stars, going after anything and everything. I think I kind of shocked myself a little bit by running those two 9.7s at the nationals because although I was prepared to run fast, I wasn’t prepared to do it then.“So it’s proven to myself that I can run very fast, even though I’m not 100% perfect with my first 30 (metres), which was a super exciting thing. So there’s a lot more to come for 2027 and 2028.”The competitive absence of Lyles is undoubtedly a blow to an event World Athletics has billed as ‘the best of the best’ with a record $10m prize purse on offer. But there’s still a lot on the programme to keep athletics fans hooked, the 1500m race in particular one of the event’s top attractions, seeing as it is set to reignite the rivalry between Great Britain’s Josh Kerr and Norway’s Jakob Ingebrigtsen.Ingebrigtsen’s recent criticism of Kerr for skipping the European Championships last month may well have added a layer of spice to their upcoming showdown. “Always under criticism,” Kerr, who clocked 3:42.66 in the mile at the London Diamond League in July to break Hicham El Guerrouj’s 27-year-old world record, said with a wry chuckle in response to his fierce rival’s comments.“Every person is different, and every athlete is different in the way that they approach the season. For me, the way that I approach it is circling two to four big dates and working my way around those and also to get in and out of a year without massive problems,” added the Scot, who won the 1500m gold at the 2023 world championships in Budapest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India demolish Pakistan 19-0 to storm into Women’s Hockey Junior Asia Cup semi-finals
articles.summary: Hockey News: India booked their place in the semi-finals of the 2026 Women’s Junior Asia Cup after beating Pakistan 19-0 in the quarter-final in Moqi, China, on Th.
articles.body: India booked their place in the semi-finals of the 2026 Women’s Junior Asia Cup after beating Pakistan 19-0 in the quarter-final in Moqi, China, on Thursday.The defending champions had already topped their group after beating Japan, Malaysia and South Korea. They will now face the winner of the South Korea vs Malaysia quarter-final for a place in the final.India took the lead in the seventh minute through Puja Sahoo and continued to score throughout the match. Roshni Aind doubled the lead two minutes later before Tanushree Dinesh Kadu, Sukhveer Kaur and Sanika Chandrakant Mane added more goals.Mane scored again in the 23rd minute, while Tanuja Toppo, Pooja Malik and Purnima Yadav also found the net before half-time. India went into the break 10-0 ahead.The goals continued after the restart. Malik completed her hat-trick with goals in the 49th and 51st minutes, while Supriya scored twice. Krishna Sharma, Binima Dhan and Roshni also added to Pakistan's problems, with Roshni scoring again in the final minute to complete the 19-0 win.India are now two wins away from completing a hat-trick of Women’s Junior Asia Cup titles.
